question: A utility starts a CMOM program for its sanitary sewers. Which record set forms the starting inventory for the program?
correctAnswer: Mapped sewers, manholes, lift stations and their known condition notes
explanation: A CMOM program begins with a documented inventory of collection assets and their condition so capacity, management, operation and maintenance work can be planned.
options: Recent water billing totals grouped by customer class and route
Mapped sewers, manholes, lift stations and their known condition notes
Vendor price lists for pumps, pipe materials and cleaning nozzles
Daily weather logs collected from the nearest airport station
optionA: Recent water billing totals grouped by customer class and route
optionB: Mapped sewers, manholes, lift stations and their known condition notes
optionC: Vendor price lists for pumps, pipe materials and cleaning nozzles
optionD: Daily weather logs collected from the nearest airport station
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: A crew schedules condition assessment for an older trunk sewer. Which input most directly sets the inspection priority?
correctAnswer: Age, material, past failures and consequence of a failure there

options: Age, material, past failures and consequence of a failure there
Colour of the pipe, depth of cover and distance from the depot
Crew preference, truck availability and time left in the shift
Number of service laterals painted on the road surface nearby
optionA: Age, material, past failures and consequence of a failure there
optionB: Colour of the pipe, depth of cover and distance from the depot
optionC: Crew preference, truck availability and time left in the shift

Fuel level of the truck, hose length and reel serial number

question: Before a worker enters a manhole for assessment, which step comes first in the entry sequence?
correctAnswer: Test the atmosphere and ventilate the space before any entry
explanation: Manholes are confined spaces, so atmospheric testing and ventilation precede entry, with rescue arrangements in place before anyone goes down.
options: Remove the benching and channel material for a clearer view
Lower the tools and camera equipment into the space first
Test the atmosphere and ventilate the space before any entry
Send one worker down briefly to check conditions by feel
optionA: Remove the benching and channel material for a clearer view
optionB: Lower the tools and camera equipment into the space first
optionC: Test the atmosphere and ventilate the space before any entry
optionD: Send one worker down briefly to check conditions by feel

question: In cured in place pipe lining, which component gives the finished liner its structural strength?
correctAnswer: The resin, once cured, bonded within the felt or fibre tube
explanation: The tube carries the resin into place, and curing hardens the resin so the tube and resin act together as a new pipe within the host pipe.
options: The calibration hose left inside the pipe after installation
The resin, once cured, bonded within the felt or fibre tube
The bypass pumping line laid along the surface during curing
The cleaning water recycled through the segment before lining
optionA: The calibration hose left inside the pipe after installation
optionB: The resin, once cured, bonded within the felt or fibre tube
optionC: The bypass pumping line laid along the surface during curing
optionD: The cleaning water recycled through the segment before lining

options: The bursting head, which fractures the old pipe as it advances
The winch cable, which pulls the new pipe at constant speed
The guide rods, which steer the head through the old pipe
The fusion machine, which joins the new pipe lengths together
optionA: The bursting head, which fractures the old pipe as it advances
optionB: The winch cable, which pulls the new pipe at constant speed
optionC: The guide rods, which steer the head through the old pipe
optionD: The fusion machine, which joins the new pipe lengths together

Average chlorine residual, calculated from depth and travel time
Average daily flow, calculated from depth, velocity and pipe area

A flat line through the storm, then a sudden drop afterward
A rapid rise soon after rain starts, then a fairly quick fall
A steady decline before rain starts, then no change at all
optionA: A slow rise days after rain ends, then a very gradual fall
optionB: A flat line through the storm, then a sudden drop afterward
optionC: A rapid rise soon after rain starts, then a fairly quick fall
optionD: A steady decline before rain starts, then no change at all

question: CCTV shows roots entering at several joints in a clay sewer that also surcharges in wet weather. What is the best next step?

Replace the whole street main before checking any other defect
Increase cleaning frequency and close the file for five years

optionB: Replace the whole street main before checking any other defect

question: An assessment finds heavy black corrosion on the concrete crown of a manhole below a force main discharge. What does this pattern indicate?
correctAnswer: Hydrogen sulfide released at the discharge is attacking the concrete
explanation: Turbulent discharge strips hydrogen sulfide from the wastewater, and the gas oxidizes to acid on moist concrete above the flow line, causing crown corrosion.
options: Road salt tracked in from the surface is staining the concrete
Hard water deposits are building up on the concrete over time
Hydrogen sulfide released at the discharge is attacking the concrete
Sunlight entering the open cover is bleaching the concrete dark
optionA: Road salt tracked in from the surface is staining the concrete
optionB: Hard water deposits are building up on the concrete over time
optionC: Hydrogen sulfide released at the discharge is attacking the concrete
optionD: Sunlight entering the open cover is bleaching the concrete dark

options: The liner enlarges the pipe and adds a new access chamber too
The liner seals the joints and stops infiltration without digging
The liner removes the need to clean or inspect the pipe first
The liner lets the crew skip bypass pumping during the work
optionA: The liner enlarges the pipe and adds a new access chamber too
optionB: The liner seals the joints and stops infiltration without digging
optionC: The liner removes the need to clean or inspect the pipe first
optionD: The liner lets the crew skip bypass pumping during the work

Spot repair at each joint along the full length of the sewer
Chemical grouting of every joint and lateral in the segment

Both basins equally, since storm size was the same for each one
Basin A, since its larger response signals more rainfall entry points
Neither basin, since peaking factors cannot guide field work

correctAnswer: Install end seals at the liner terminations in each manhole
explanation: Annular space at liner ends is a known leakage path, and hydrophilic or mechanical end seals close it where the liner meets the manhole.
options: Extend the curing time so the liner hardens more at the ends
Install end seals at the liner terminations in each manhole
Raise the bypass pumping rate during the next installation
Cut the liner shorter so it ends inside the pipe barrel
optionA: Extend the curing time so the liner hardens more at the ends
optionB: Install end seals at the liner terminations in each manhole
optionC: Raise the bypass pumping rate during the next installation
optionD: Cut the liner shorter so it ends inside the pipe barrel

Fill the sewer with water so the head stays centred in the pipe

The grout for the annulus will cure too slowly in oval pipe
The winch will use more fuel pulling through deformed pipe
The fused pipe string will be too light to sink in the flow

correctAnswer: Overflow history, condition grades and flows tied to specific assets

question: Two segments share the same structural grade. One lies under a hospital access road, the other under a quiet lane. How does the program rank them?
correctAnswer: The hospital road segment ranks higher on consequence of failure
explanation: Risk combines likelihood with consequence. Equal grades mean equal likelihood, so the segment whose failure disrupts a critical route ranks first.
options: The hospital road segment ranks higher on consequence of failure
The quiet lane segment ranks higher, since access is easier there
Both rank the same, since the structural grades are identical
The newer segment ranks higher, since its data is more current
optionA: The hospital road segment ranks higher on consequence of failure
optionB: The quiet lane segment ranks higher, since access is easier there
optionC: Both rank the same, since the structural grades are identical
optionD: The newer segment ranks higher, since its data is more current

question: CCTV grades a sewer as moderate, yet it has blocked three times in a year from grease. Which conclusion should the operator draw?
correctAnswer: Structural grade alone misses the operational defect driving failures
explanation: CCTV structural scoring does not capture service performance. Repeated grease blockages call for cleaning frequency changes and source control, not just structural repair.
options: The blockages prove the CCTV grade was recorded incorrectly
Grease blockages mean the pipe has already failed structurally
Cleaning records and CCTV grades should never be compared
Structural grade alone misses the operational defect driving failures
optionA: The blockages prove the CCTV grade was recorded incorrectly
optionB: Grease blockages mean the pipe has already failed structurally
optionC: Cleaning records and CCTV grades should never be compared
optionD: Structural grade alone misses the operational defect driving failures

question: Several manholes on one street show the same chimney leakage and ponded covers. Which program level response fits this pattern?
correctAnswer: Treat it as a street wide defect pattern in the renewal program

Record each case separately with no link between the files

Lower the street cleaning frequency to reduce surface water

question: A lined sewer still shows high infiltration at the lateral connections after lining. Which limitation of CIPP explains this?
correctAnswer: Standard lining seals the main but leaves lateral junctions open
explanation: A mainline liner covers the barrel, and unless lateral seals or top hat liners are added, groundwater still enters at each unsealed lateral connection.
options: The liner resin loses strength when laterals are reconnected
Standard lining seals the main but leaves lateral junctions open
Robotic cutters cannot reopen laterals after the liner cures
Lateral flow is too small to measure after the main is lined
optionA: The liner resin loses strength when laterals are reconnected
optionB: Standard lining seals the main but leaves lateral junctions open

question: Ground heave is reported on a lawn above a bursting run in dense clay. Which job condition most likely contributed?
correctAnswer: Upsizing the pipe in soil that cannot absorb the displaced volume
explanation: Bursting displaces soil equal to the size increase. In dense, confined soils that volume can push upward as heave instead of compressing outward.
options: Upsizing the pipe in soil that cannot absorb the displaced volume
Pulling the new pipe too slowly through the host pipe run
Using a lubricant on the bursting head during the long run
Fusing the pipe string on the surface before the pull began
optionA: Upsizing the pipe in soil that cannot absorb the displaced volume
optionB: Pulling the new pipe too slowly through the host pipe run
optionC: Using a lubricant on the bursting head during the long run
optionD: Fusing the pipe string on the surface before the pull began

question: Monitors above and below a reach differ by 12 L/s at night, with no branches between them. What does the difference localize?
correctAnswer: Infiltration entering along that single reach of sewer pipe
explanation: A flow balance between bracketing monitors isolates gains to the reach between them, here a steady night gain consistent with infiltration in that reach.
options: Industrial discharge entering from a plant on the reach bank
Rainfall inflow entering through covers along the whole basin
Meter error, since two monitors should always read the same
Infiltration entering along that single reach of sewer pipe
optionA: Industrial discharge entering from a plant on the reach bank
optionB: Rainfall inflow entering through covers along the whole basin
optionC: Meter error, since two monitors should always read the same
optionD: Infiltration entering along that single reach of sewer pipe

question: Winter melt in March produces high sewer flows with no rain recorded. How should the RDII program classify this event?
correctAnswer: Snowmelt driven inflow and infiltration, tracked as its own pattern
explanation: Meltwater reaches sewers through the same inflow and infiltration paths as rain, often over longer durations, so western programs track melt response separately.
options: Dry weather flow, since the rain gauge recorded no rainfall
A monitor fault, since high flows require recorded rainfall
Snowmelt driven inflow and infiltration, tracked as its own pattern
Industrial discharge, since melt events follow plant schedules
optionA: Dry weather flow, since the rain gauge recorded no rainfall
optionB: A monitor fault, since high flows require recorded rainfall
optionC: Snowmelt driven inflow and infiltration, tracked as its own pattern
optionD: Industrial discharge, since melt events follow plant schedules
